entries.name: ball lightning
entries.senseHere: A short-lived glowing sphere seen during or near thunderstorms, lasting seconds and vanishing with or without leaving a mark. Its cause is still unexplained, and the term covers a wide range of reported shapes, colours, sizes, and behaviours rather than one agreed phenomenon.

entries.name: fragmented science
entries.senseHere: A label for ball lightning research describing how work on the topic is scattered across unconnected individuals and small groups, with no shared data, agreed methods, or unifying theory holding it together.

entries.name: COST Action
entries.background: A European-funded research collaboration programme that brings scientists from different countries together on a shared topic without itself funding the research directly.

entries.name: ALDIS
aliases: Austrian lightning detection and information system
entries.senseHere: Austria's network for detecting and locating lightning strikes, used in this article to check whether reported ball lightning sightings line up in time and place with real recorded lightning strokes.

entries.name: BLIDS
entries.senseHere: Germany's lightning detection and location network, used alongside Austria's ALDIS to match ball lightning reports against recorded strikes.

entries.name: Cavendish Laboratory
entries.background: The physics department of Cambridge University, long one of the world's leading centres for experimental physics, where discoveries such as the electron and the structure of DNA were made.

entries.name: keraunoparalysis
entries.senseHere: A short-lived paralysis or numbness in part of the body caused by being near a lightning or ball lightning strike, as distinct from longer-lasting nerve damage or psychological trauma from the same event.
